subject: Engineering Fundamentals
title: The Banqiao Dam Failure
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on The Banqiao Dam Failure.

hook.text: On August 7, 1975, the Banqiao Dam in China burst during Typhoon Nina. An estimated 170,000 people died.

buildup.text: The dam was designed for a 1-in-1,000-year flood. Typhoon Nina delivered a 1-in-2,000-year rainfall in 24 hours.

discovery.text: Sluice gates were clogged with sediment. Water couldn't be released fast enough, and the reservoir overtopped the dam.

twist.text: Hydrologist Chen Xing had warned about the design flaws years earlier. He was removed from the project for being too cautious.

climax.text: China reformed its dam safety standards and now maintains the world's most extensive dam monitoring network.

punchline.text: The engineer who warned them was silenced. The dam agreed with him.

quiz.question: Why couldn't the Banqiao Dam handle Typhoon Nina's rainfall?
options: The dam was only 10 years old and the concrete hadn't fully cured
Sluice gates were clogged with sediment and couldn't release water fast enough
The typhoon's wind destroyed the dam's structural reinforcement
